messages:
jane_customer: Hey team — our app is getting truncated streaming responses from Redwood. Long completions will stream for ~40-60s then stop mid-token. Client reconnects and we see a new stream but the rest of the tokens are lost. Help?
maria_support: sorry about that :frowning: can you paste a minimal repro (curl or fetch) + headers you're hitting through (ALB / NLB / Cloudflare / plain nginx)?
jane_customer: repro: `curl -N -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer <key>\" https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams/chat` then we get: `data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"content":"Hello wor"}}]}` then connection closes. No final event. We're behind an ALB + Cloudflare.
jane_customer: logs show TLS close from ALB around 60s: `FIN from 10.0.5.12: downstream idle timeout`
noah_backend: thanks. Two likely things: 1) ALB idle timeout defaults to 60s and will close if there's no data for that TCP flow; 2) Cloudflare (and some proxies) can buffer or coalesce chunks and suppress small keepalive chunks. If your generator pauses between tokens for >60s, ALB may close and client sees truncated stream.
lee_edge: also check intermediate HTTP/2 windowing and Envoy/nginx buffer settings — some proxies won't flush single small SSE frames. nginx: `proxy_buffering off; proxy_cache off; chunked_transfer_encoding on; sendfile off; tcp_nodelay on;` helps. For Envoy check `flush_interval` and `stream_idle_timeout` behavior.
maria_support: can you share the server side pattern? Are you sending a single `\n\n` heartbeat or anything? If not, you can either: (A) emit periodic SSE comments `: keepalive\n\n` every 15s, or (B) increase ALB idle timeout to exceed your longest pause. Both recommended.
jane_customer: we don't emit heartbeats currently. Our model sometimes stalls ~70s on long context. Can we get ALB changed? We're on managed infra.
alex_sre: tagging infra. @infra-team could we temporarily bump the ALB idle timeout for customer-redwood-target-group to 300s while they implement heartbeats?
sre-bot: infra ticket created: #INC-4529 — requested ALB idle timeout change for target group tg-0a1b2c. ETA: 2 business days.
maria_support: in parallel please try a quick local repro to confirm behavior: 1) run `socat -d -d TCP4-LISTEN:8080,fork SYSTEM:"printf 'HTTP/1.1 200 OK\\r\\nContent-Type: text/event-stream\\r\\nTransfer-Encoding: chunked\\r\\n\\r\\n'; sleep 70; printf '10\r\n: keepalive\\n\\r\\n\r\n'` 2) curl -N to that endpoint through same path. If curl is cut at ~60s we reproduced ALB idle close.
noah_backend: additional note — if you're behind Cloudflare in front of ALB, Cloudflare has its own 100s idle timeout on long polling. If Cloudflare is proxying (not in passthrough TCP mode), heartbeats are required. For customers using ALB + Cloudflare we'd recommend heartbeats + ALB timeout >= 2x heartbeat interval.
jane_customer: did the socat test, confirmed it drops ~60s. good repro. Any config we can change in our app now to reduce token loss?
lee_edge: server-side quick fix: send a SSE comment every 15s: `: ping\n\n` (this is valid SSE and very small). Also ensure you write and flush (call `fflush` / `res.flush()` depending on framework) after each SSE event — otherwise proxy buffering will hold it.
maria_support: we also recommend adding an idempotency layer on the client so reconnects can resume from the last accepted token (sequence IDs in events). That prevents semantic loss if a connection is interrupted mid-response.
alex_sre: infra updated ALB idle timeout to 300s for the customer's target group (rolled at 2026-03-16T18:10Z) as a stopgap. Please validate.
jane_customer: after ALB change + adding SSE `: ping` every 15s and explicit flush, streaming is stable in our staging. No truncations for >10m now. Thanks!
maria_support: great — next steps summarized: 1) keep heartbeats in server (15s recommended), 2) flush after each event, 3) add client resume/seq ids, 4) infra to keep ALB timeout >= 300s or use NLB_TCP passthrough if you want pure TCP with longer idle. We'll close the ticket after 48h stable.
noah_backend: FYI added a short doc snippet to internal KB: `support/streaming-proxy-guidance` with examples for nginx/envoy/ALB/Cloudflare and an SSE ping snippet. Link in ticket.
jane_customer: appreciated :raised_hands: reopening if anything else crops up.
maria_support: marking resolved unless we see recurrence. :white_check_mark:
